title: Queueing Theory Bank Simulation
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D queueing theory bank simulation using Three.js (CDN). The scene simulates an M/M/c queue (Poisson arrivals, exponential service times, c tellers).

## Scene Setup
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera at (0, 18, 22) looking at origin, FOV 55.
- Lighting: Ambient light (0xffffff, 0.5) + DirectionalLight (0xffffff, 0.8) at (10, 20, 10).
- Floor: Large plane (40x30) with a light beige material (0xf5f0e1) representing the bank floor.
- Walls: Three thin box geometries forming the back and side walls, colored (0xd4c5a9).
- Teller counters: 3 box geometries (width 3, height 1.2, depth 1) placed side by side along the back wall at z=-8, colored (0x8B4513). Each has a small sphere (0x00ff00 = available, 0xff0000 = busy) floating above it as a status indicator.
- Queue area: Render rope stanchions (cylinder pairs with a catenary line between them) forming a serpentine queue path from the entrance (z=10) toward the counters.
- Customers: Capsule geometries (radius 0.3, height 1.2) with random pastel colors. They move along the queue path toward the next available teller.

## Simulation Parameters (stored in window.__3D_STATE__)
- arrivalRate: 2.0 (customers per second, lambda). Adjustable via UI slider (0.5 to 5.0).
- serviceRate: 1.0 (customers per second per teller, mu). Adjustable via UI slider (0.2 to 3.0).
- numTellers: 3 (adjustable via +/- buttons, range 1-5).
- simulationSpeed: 1.0 (adjustable via slider, 0.1 to 5.0).
- running: boolean, starts false.

## Queueing Mechanics
- Customers arrive following a Poisson process (exponential inter-arrival times with rate lambda).
- Each customer joins the back of a single shared FIFO queue.
- When a teller becomes free, the front customer in the queue moves to that teller.
- Service time is exponentially distributed with rate mu.
- After service, the customer walks toward the exit (z=14) and is removed from the scene.
- Customers in the queue animate smoothly toward the front as the line advances.

## Statistics Tracking (all in window.__3D_STATE__)
- totalArrivals: count of all customers who arrived.
- totalServed: count of all customers who completed service.
- totalInSystem: current number of customers (in queue + being served).
- queueLength: current number waiting in queue (not being served).
- avgWaitTime: running average wait time in queue (seconds of sim time).
- avgServiceTime: running average service time (seconds of sim time).
- serverUtilization: fraction of tellers currently busy (0 to 1).
- theoreticalAvgWait: computed from M/M/c formula using Erlang-C.
- tellerStates: array of objects [{id, busy, customersServed}] for each teller.
- customers: array of {id, state, queuePosition, assignedTeller, waitTime, serviceTime} for each active customer. state is 'waiting', 'serving', or 'leaving'.
- simTime: total elapsed simulation time in seconds.
- throughput: totalServed / simTime.

## User Interactions
- Start/Pause button (id='btn-start-pause'): toggles window.__3D_STATE__.running. Text shows 'Start' or 'Pause'.
- Reset button (id='btn-reset'): stops simulation, removes all customers, resets all stats to 0/initial.
- Arrival rate slider (id='slider-arrival'): updates arrivalRate in real time.
- Service rate slider (id='slider-service'): updates serviceRate in real time.
- Speed slider (id='slider-speed'): updates simulationSpeed.
- Teller + button (id='btn-teller-add'): adds a teller (max 5), spawns new counter geometry.
- Teller - button (id='btn-teller-remove'): removes last teller (min 1), removes counter geometry. If teller was serving, customer goes back to front of queue.
- Click on a teller counter: highlights it and shows that teller's stats in a tooltip div (id='teller-tooltip').
- Keyboard 'Space': toggle start/pause. 'R': reset. '+'/'-': adjust tellers.

## HUD / UI
- Top-left panel (id='stats-panel') showing: Queue Length, Total In System, Avg Wait Time, Server Utilization, Throughput, Theoretical Avg Wait (Erlang-C).
- Bottom control bar with all sliders and buttons.
- All numeric displays update every animation frame.

## State Object
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with ALL fields listed above. Update every frame. Ensure all numeric values are never NaN or Infinity (clamp/default to 0).
physics_constraints: Poisson arrival process with exponential inter-arrival times. Exponential service times. M/M/c queueing discipline (FIFO). Little's Law must approximately hold: L ≈ λ * W where L = avg number in system, λ = effective arrival rate, W = avg time in system. Server utilization ρ = λ / (c * μ) must stay between 0 and 1 for stable queue. All statistics must be NaN-free and non-negative. Customer counts must be conserved: totalArrivals = totalServed + totalInSystem at all times.
